A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the static simulation results show that Japan's existing FTAS have a limited impact on the economy and trade.
the static and dynamic simulations in this paper show that the impacts of an FTA are not necessarily positive.
the results show that the static and dynamic impacts of the existing FTAs are not very large, and the welfare gains of an FTA with the US and agricultural liberalization are not very large either.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Japan's existing bilateral free trade agreements (FTAs) have a limited impact on its economy, but that Japan's future FTAs with the United States, the EU and ASEAN would have a much greater impact.
FTAs can have significant effects on the Japanese economy and that their effects vary depending on the partner countries and on the structure of the FTAs themselves.
FTAs are likely to increase the welfare of the participating countries, but the magnitude is not very large.
